purpose: Post-call Analysis setup for judging elite Atlas Web Studio voice-agent behavior and collecting structured call data.

success_evaluation.unknown_policy: Return unknown when the transcript does not contain the buyer move needed to judge the criterion.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Business-impact answers should use commercial mechanism before caveat and name a concrete buyer action.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: The answer starts with a commercial mechanism, ties it to a buyer action such as calling, booking, requesting a quote, checking services, checking policies, checking reviews, or choosing from Maps, and keeps the caveat precise.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The answer leads with generic caveats, vague clarity language, or abstract online-presence value without naming what the buyer can do.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No business-impact question or answer appears in the transcript.
edge_cases: If the buyer explicitly asks for a guarantee, a boundary may come first.
If the answer uses clearer page/homepage/path, it must be supporting language tied to a concrete action.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: General business-impact questions should not open with not-as-a-guarantee wording.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: The answer opens with mechanism first unless the buyer asked for a guarantee.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The answer opens with 'Not as a guarantee', 'I can't promise', or equivalent when the buyer asked general business impact rather than a guarantee.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No general business-impact or guarantee question appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Soft agreements are not send commitments.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: A buyer phrase such as 'that makes sense', 'I get it', 'that's interesting', 'fair enough', or 'okay, I see what you mean' triggers a soft send question such as 'Want me to send the mockup so you can judge it?' If Emma's immediately previous turn already invited the buyer to see the mockup, a brief bridge such as 'Yeah, exactly. I can send it over - best email?' is allowed.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The agent asks for email after unrelated soft agreement, starts the two-step close without a send signal, treats soft agreement as accepted mockup, repeats a full CTA after already inviting the mockup, or asks the same send-permission question again after the buyer softens.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No soft agreement appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Clear send signals without an email should trigger concise email capture.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: A send signal such as 'send it over', 'I'll take a look', 'go ahead', 'can I see it', 'how do I see it', or 'where do I see it' appears before any email and triggers one concise email question such as 'Best email?', 'What's the best email?', or 'Where should I send it?'
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The agent continues discovery, re-pitches value, fails to ask for an approved send path after a clear send signal, asks for the best email after the buyer already provided one, or asks again whether to send after the buyer says 'okay, send it', 'go ahead', 'fine, send it', or 'send it over'.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No accepted-mockup send signal without an email appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Email delivery should use the natural two-step confirmation and close.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: After a clear email, the agent confirms the normalized email only; after buyer confirmation, the agent closes naturally in one short line with by the end of the day delivery timing.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The agent asks for the best email after an email was already provided, skips email confirmation after receiving a reachable next turn, says it will send before confirmation, continues discovery, re-pitches, over-explains reply path, uses the wrong delivery timing, leaks follow-up language, or fails to close after confirmation.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: The buyer never gives an email, or the transcript ends immediately after email before the agent has a chance to respond.
edge_cases: If the buyer gives an email and confirms it in the same turn, a one-turn close is acceptable.
If the buyer asks whether they can reply, a brief yes is acceptable.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Gatekeepers should get short note or callback handling without a full pitch.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: The agent asks for owner reachability or gives the short Atlas note, confirms a callback window when provided, and closes after ok/got it.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The agent pitches the full value proposition, asks the gatekeeper to evaluate the offer, adds extra pitch details after callback, or restarts selling after ok/got it.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No gatekeeper or wrong-person exchange appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Local SEO answers should be confident and non-guaranteed.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: The answer says the goal is local search foundation or gives Google a proper page to read, names services/location/service area/photos/reviews/call or booking info, and avoids ranking, traffic, customer, call, booking, or numerical lift guarantees.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The answer guarantees rankings, traffic, customers, calls, bookings, patients, jobs, revenue, or page-one placement.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No SEO or local-search question appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Cost answers should explain real project complexity drivers.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: The answer gives a relevant range by the first or second direct price ask when campaign facts allow one, maps the request to a complexity band, distinguishes basic site, light feature or premium one-page, workflow/content-heavy, integration-heavy, and fully custom scoped work when relevant, says the range is a ballpark rather than a final quote, and gives one relevant range instead of the whole menu. For CRM/payment/calendar questions, Emma answers capability first before price. For custom portal/dashboard, Emma uses scoped-pricing language first and names concrete drivers such as secure login, user accounts, database, permissions, security, cloud setup, integrations, testing, or ongoing maintenance.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail if the buyer asks about a specific feature twice and Emma gives no range, gives only 'it depends' without cost drivers, repeats free mockup/no obligation instead of answering cost, reaches max turns because Emma avoided price, gives a fixed feature price as if guaranteed, says quote filtering is always exactly $3,000, says we don't do filtering, dumps the whole pricing menu when buyer asked about one feature, jumps into price before answering a capability question clearly, quotes a clean $4,000-$5,000 range for custom portal/dashboard before scoped caveat, forces beyond $5k language when the buyer did not ask about the normal/high-end range, quotes a final fixed price for custom work without scope, invents unsupported numbers outside approved ranges, implies SEO/calls/jobs/revenue/rankings are guaranteed, or only lists vague drivers such as significant development time or expertise.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No price, cost, or scope-driver question appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Buyer-facing agent responses must not contain bracketed internal labels.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: No agent response contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: any response contains a bracketed label such as an emotion, pacing note, stage label, sales label, policy label, source label, tone tag, or similar internal marker.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: Transcript does not include agent response text.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Repeated status-quo challenges should trigger value-angle rotation or clean disqualification.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: If the buyer challenges the same issue multiple times, Emma uses a different mechanism or disqualifies.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma repeats the same value angle or creates a residue loop: the same core point with different words after the buyer asks again, instead of rotating mechanism, answering the missing point, asking one forward-moving question, or disqualifying a guarantee-only buyer.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No repeated challenge appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Clarification turns should sound natural and not echo canned examples.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: Examples are varied naturally, and clarification answers use a fresh concrete mechanism tied to the buyer's business.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma repeats the same canned phrase across multiple turns, repeats 'Fair point - the practical difference is...' more than once in a call, produces an AI monologue, or keeps restating the same residue loop when the buyer asks for clarification.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No clarification or repeated-question turn appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Emma should avoid CTA fatigue while still making one natural first-call next-step move when the buyer remains open.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: Emma does not repeatedly ask to send the mockup or ask for email after unresolved process-risk questions. After answering the buyer's main concern, if the buyer is not stop/gatekeeper-only/wrong-person/guarantee-only/refusing/terminal and no email has been captured, Emma makes one low-friction next-step move such as 'Want me to send the mockup so you can judge it?' or 'I can show that in the mockup - best email?'
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: Emma asks to send the mockup more than twice without a new buyer commitment, asks for email during process-risk or price questions, asks for email repeatedly, asks the same CTA/email question repeatedly without a new buyer commitment, repeats 'Would you like me to send it?' after the buyer has already softened or accepted, answers several non-terminal buyer questions but never attempts one natural close, or lets an open buyer leave after price/process info with no send invitation.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: Transcript does not include repeated CTA opportunities or process-risk pushback.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Process-risk questions must be answered before email capture.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: When buyer asks process-risk questions, Emma clarifies the process and only asks for email after a clear send signal.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: Emma asks for email during process-risk objections before clear consent, or while the buyer is still asking what happens next, whether there will be pressure, or whether there will be calls.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No process-risk question appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Post-mockup path defaults to buyer email reply, with no automatic call, check-back, follow-up, or later reach-out.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: Emma uses the buyer-reply email path or says no automatic call after, and does not offer or imply follow-up unless the buyer asks for or agrees to a callback.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: Emma says 'I can follow up later', 'I'll check back', 'I'll call after you review it', 'We'll follow up', 'I'll reach out later', or equivalent without buyer permission.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No post-mockup follow-up, email-reply path, or callback claim appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Headline value should be a concrete website mechanism, not generic web-presence or conversion language.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: Emma leads with a concrete mechanism such as tap-to-call, quote request, service-area check, emergency-service check, price/policy FAQ, DM reduction, trust-before-call, local search foundation, after-hours answer page, comparison page, appointment request, or call path. Weak headline phrases such as professional homepage, visual representation, online presence, fresh perspective, potential design/layout, or We specialize pass only when used once as support after a concrete mechanism, a precise mockup-scope explanation, or natural language tied to a buyer action.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma uses weak generic headline value such as online presence, refreshed online presence, clearer online experience, potential improvements, professional homepage, professional website, visual representation, fresh perspective, potential design/layout, organized information, central hub, online brochure, convert visitors into customers, more engagement, better engagement, inquiries, more inquiries, help patients find your services, help people understand your services, help customers find your services, easier to take the next step, We specialize, or similar wording as the headline value, generic opening pitch, stale-script filler, repeated brochure language, or replacement for concrete buyer-action value. Hard fail for an unrequested long feature dump.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No value answer appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Guarantee-only buyers should get a safe boundary and clean disqualification.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: Emma says nobody can honestly guarantee page-one SEO, rankings, fixed calls, or jobs; warns to be careful with anyone selling it that way; distinguishes local search foundation/site experience from guarantees; triggers the guarantee-only lock when guarantees are required; and disqualifies without repeated repitching.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma implies guaranteed SEO/calls, invents past proof, overpromises, calls every competitor a scam, keeps selling after the guarantee-only disqualification lock, asks to send the mockup after guarantee-only disqualification, asks 'Are you still there?', asks 'Is there anything else I can help you with today?', asks 'Would you still like the mockup?', asks 'Can I send you something anyway?', or keeps repitching after guarantee-only disqualification.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No guarantee-demand exchange appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Guarantee-only bad-fit buyers should not get a reopened pitch after the lock is triggered.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: When the buyer makes guaranteed calls, jobs, rankings, page-one SEO, or outcomes a condition, Emma gives one safe boundary or clarification, says Atlas is not the right fit if guarantees are required, and closes without another mockup CTA.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail if a guarantee-only buyer receives any mockup pitch after lock. Also fail if Emma asks to send the mockup, asks for email, asks 'Are you still there?', asks 'Is there anything else I can help you with today?', asks 'Would you still like the mockup?', asks 'Can I send you something anyway?', explains new value angles, talks about better engagement, online presence, customer journey, potential customers, inquiries, clearer website, free mockup, or otherwise re-opens the pitch after guarantee-only disqualification.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No guarantee-only disqualification condition appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Emma should use the buyer's real action path instead of forcing booking or appointment language.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: For HVAC, plumbing, electrical, or auto repair, Emma uses call, quote request, estimate request, service area, emergency service, diagnostics, hours, location, or tap-to-call language. Dental is appointment request or call without patient-growth claims; salon booking appears only when appropriate.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma says booking, appointments, appointment booking, or online booking for a call-driven vertical after the buyer says they do not use online booking, or uses patient-growth language for dental.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No vertical-specific action path appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Emma should not ask for known business context.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: If business_name is already known from variables or transcript, Emma does not ask for the business name. When buyer asks what is needed, Emma says 'I've got enough for the first version...' and asks for one optional highlight or, after acceptance, the email.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma asks for the business name when business_name is already known, asks for basic known business context instead of the next useful missing field after acceptance, says 'I already have {{business_name}} and the business type', says 'I already have your online information', says 'I already looked you up', or says 'I already have information about you'.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No known business context or what-is-needed question appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Spoken email addresses should be normalized in confirmation and data extraction.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: For realistic spoken emails, the extracted email field and agent confirmation normalize at and dot phrasing into an address such as service@northsideautorepair.com, info@summithvac.com, lunahairstudio@email.com, or luna.hair.studio.tampa@email.com.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma asks for email again after the buyer already gave it, fails to confirm the destination, changes the email incorrectly, confirms only an unnormalized spoken at/dot form when a normalized form is clear, or Analysis leaves a realistic spoken email unnormalized.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No realistic spoken email appears, or the transcript ends immediately after email before Emma can respond.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: A guarantee-only first buyer turn should lock immediately instead of receiving a mockup pitch.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: If the first buyer turn requires guaranteed page-one SEO, emergency calls, more calls, jobs, patients, rankings, traffic, revenue, or outcomes, Emma says nobody can honestly guarantee those outcomes, warns to be careful with anyone selling guaranteed rankings or calls, names local search foundation and site experience as the helpable scope, says Atlas is probably not the right fit if the guarantee is required, and does not pitch the mockup.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: a guarantee-only first turn gets a mockup pitch, send CTA, email request, new value angle, online presence language, customer journey language, potential customers language, inquiries language, better engagement language, clearer website language, free mockup pitch, or continued selling instead of the guarantee lock.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: The transcript does not start with a guarantee-only buyer condition.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Runtime output must not leak bracketed tone, style, or internal control tags.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: No agent response contains bracketed tone, emotion, pacing, stage, sales, policy, source, or internal tags.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: any buyer-facing agent response contains a bracketed runtime tone tag or internal label.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: Transcript does not include agent response text.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Mockup delivery timing should use the campaign's end-of-day timing.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: After confirmed email, Emma says the mockup will be sent by the end of the day.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: Emma says the mockup will arrive soon, shortly, in a few days, within a few business days, or gives a timing that conflicts with by the end of the day.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No email-confirmed close or delivery-timing question appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: The default post-mockup follow-up path is buyer reply to the email.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: When closing after email confirmation, Emma either naturally mentions that the buyer can reply to that email if anything looks off or keeps the close short without implying an automatic callback.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma claims she will call, follow up, check back, or schedule a post-mockup discussion automatically instead of using the buyer-reply email path.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No email-confirmed close appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Realistic email addresses require explicit buyer confirmation before Emma uses send language.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: When the buyer gives a realistic email, Emma confirms the normalized address and waits for explicit confirmation such as yes, correct, that is right, that is correct, yes that is the right email, that is the right place, or that email is right before any send language. If buyer gives email plus 'still free, right?', Emma answers free/no obligation briefly and confirms the normalized email before send language.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail: Emma treats a non-confirmation comment as email confirmation, says she will send before explicit confirmation, confirms only spoken at/dot form instead of the normalized address, or says send language before explicit email confirmation after buyer gives email plus 'still free, right?'. Non-confirmation comments include I will take a look when I can, I will keep an eye out, no hidden fees right, this is really free right, I am not committing to anything, just send it there, that is where you can send it, I will check it later, or send it there.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No realistic email appears, or the transcript ends before Emma has a response turn.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: A terminal goodbye should be short, natural, and not repeated.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: After a completed call outcome plus terminal cue such as 'thanks, bye', 'okay, thanks, bye', 'alright, got it, bye', or 'bye', Emma says terminal "Take care" only and stops. After 'why are you still talking', Emma may say 'You're right. Have a good one' and stop. If the buyer only says 'got it, thanks' after a non-terminal information answer and no email has been captured, Emma should not treat that as completed terminal close.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Emma keeps pitching after a completed terminal close, asks for the mockup or email after a completed terminal close, says 'You're welcome. Have a great day', says 'You're welcome. Have a good one', uses unnatural language such as 'I'm not hanging up' or 'I'll stop here', repeats goodbye more than once, adds extra explanation, continues after the terminal close, or says only 'Take care' after a non-terminal information answer when the buyer remains open and no email has been captured.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No terminal refusal, stop cue, or irritated goodbye appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Evaluation should not treat placeholder-looking contact values as real email-normalization evidence.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: Email-normalization judgments use realistic emails such as info@brightlanedental.com, brightlanedental@gmail.com, service@northsideautorepair.com, info@summithvac.com, freshnestcleaning@gmail.com, or luna.hair.studio.tampa@email.com.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: A test or analysis rationale treats placeholder-looking contact values as a real successful normalization case outside a placeholder-specific test.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No email-normalization judgment appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Emma should sound like a capable human seller.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: Responses are usually 1 to 2 short sentences, conversational, one concrete point, one natural next step, and no more than one question. A short casual transition helps after skepticism, correction, or pushback, but should not be forced every turn. 'We specialize' or similar language can pass when immediately tied to a concrete vertical/action mechanism.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: Hard fail for AI monologue, long feature dump not requested by the buyer, missing casual transition on scripted pitch turns, mechanically starts nearly every turn with the same transition, scripted/robotic/policy-like wording, overly long responses, or repeated phrases such as 'I understand your concern', 'Thanks for confirming', 'Great to connect with you', generic 'We specialize' pitch, 'enhance your online presence' as headline value, or default 'Not as a guarantee'.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: Transcript is too short to judge spoken rhythm.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: Stop or do-not-call requests end the sales motion immediately.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: The agent acknowledges the stop/do-not-call request and closes without another pitch or discovery question.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The agent keeps selling, asks for a mockup review, schedules a callback, or argues after a clear stop/do-not-call request.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: No stop, refusal, or do-not-call request appears.

success_evaluation_criteria.description: The agent must not invent proof, urgency, contacts, or guaranteed outcomes.
success_evaluation_criteria.pass: The transcript contains no invented portfolio proof, fake testimonials, fake urgency, invented contact details, or guaranteed results.
success_evaluation_criteria.failure: The agent invents proof, claims a guaranteed result, claims it already found or sent to an email it does not have, creates false urgency, or fabricates contact data.
success_evaluation_criteria.unknown: Transcript is too incomplete to judge claims.

data_collection.unknown_policy: Use null for missing strings and false for missing booleans unless the transcript clearly supports true.

data_collection_fields.name: buyer_role
data_collection_fields.description: Role of the person speaking with Emma.

data_collection_fields.name: contact_name
data_collection_fields.description: Name the buyer gives for themselves or the decision maker.

data_collection_fields.name: email
data_collection_fields.description: Normalized email address provided by the buyer.

data_collection_fields.name: callback_window
data_collection_fields.description: Specific callback timing or window provided by the buyer or gatekeeper.

data_collection_fields.name: business_name
data_collection_fields.description: Business name from variables or transcript.

data_collection_fields.name: vertical
data_collection_fields.description: Business vertical such as salon, mechanic, plumber, restaurant, dental, cleaning, HVAC, or unknown.

data_collection_fields.name: objection_type
data_collection_fields.description: Primary objection such as Instagram status quo, Google/Maps status quo, price, SEO guarantee, catch, gatekeeper, busy, or no interest.

data_collection_fields.name: value_angle_used
data_collection_fields.description: Main value mechanism Emma used, such as booking filter, quote filter, trust-before-call page, local search foundation, after-hours answer page, tap-to-call page, FAQ/price/policy filter, page people can check before calling or booking, service-area page, or comparison page.

data_collection_fields.name: accepted_mockup
data_collection_fields.description: True when the buyer clearly agrees to see or receive the mockup.

data_collection_fields.name: soft_agreement_only
data_collection_fields.description: True when the buyer only softens with phrases like that makes sense without committing to receive the mockup.

data_collection_fields.name: send_signal
data_collection_fields.description: True when the buyer asks to see, receive, or be sent the mockup. A provided email belongs to email/gave_email state, not the accepted-mockup email-capture trigger.

data_collection_fields.name: terminal_outcome
data_collection_fields.description: Final practical outcome of the call.

data_collection_fields.name: failure_reason
data_collection_fields.description: Main reason the call failed, if applicable.

data_collection_fields.name: next_step
data_collection_fields.description: Concrete next action such as send mockup, call back after 2, stop calling, or none.
